hypothesis: If the claim holds, segmented 3D surfaces of biconcave (discocyte) red blood cells have a mean curvature that varies strongly over the surface (far from constant), whereas the same measure is near-constant on spherical cells (spherocytes) in the same dataset.
pass_criterion: After meshing each segmented 3D cell and estimating per-vertex mean curvature H, the median coefficient of variation (CV = SD/|mean| of H over the surface, excluding the 5% of vertices with highest curvature to guard against segmentation noise) for discocyte-class cells is at least 0.5, and is at least 3 times the median CV for spherocyte-class cells. The discocyte CV must also exceed the CV of an ideal sphere meshed at the same voxel resolution plus 0.25. Fewer than 20 cells per class would make the test inconclusive.
fail_criterion: The median CV of H for discocyte-class cells is below 0.2, or is less than 1.5 times the median CV for spherocyte-class cells. That would mean the biconcave surface is close to constant mean curvature within measurement error, which would refute the claim.
interpretation: Thompson's 'surface of equilibrium' under surface tension alone is a surface of constant mean curvature (the Plateau/Delaunay family). The measurable quantity is the spatial variation of mean curvature on the reconstructed 3D surface of a cell. A biconcave disc has regions of negative curvature (the dimple) and positive curvature (the rim), so H cannot be constant. The 'sphere in diluted blood' corresponds to the spherocyte or swollen-sphere class. This dataset does not test the second half of the claim, that osmotic or liquid-crystal forces maintain the shape. It tests only the geometric non-equilibrium premise. It does not rule out the modern view that bending elasticity and membrane skeleton elasticity, rather than osmotic or liquid-crystal forces, set the shape. The modern reinterpretation is that cell shape is a minimum of the Helfrich bending energy with area and volume constraints, not a constant-mean-curvature surface. I have not opened the archive, so the class labels and the file format of the segmented cells still need to be checked before the analysis runs.

dataset.name: CytoShapeNet: Red blood cell phenotyping from 3D confocal images using artificial neural networks
dataset.publisher: Zenodo (Simionato, Hinkelmann, Chachanidze, Bianchi, Fermo, van Wijk, Leonetti, Wagner, Kaestner, Quint)
dataset.why_it_fits: The record has downloadable code and data (data.7z.001 to .010, about 10 GB) supporting a PLoS Comput Biol 2021 paper on 3D confocal images of red blood cells. According to the paper, the cells are classed by morphology, including discocytes, stomatocytes, echinocytes and spherocytes. I confirmed the title, authors and file list on the Zenodo page. The page does not describe the contents of the data archives, so the class labels per cell are not confirmed. The fields to use are the segmented 3D cell volumes (or surfaces) and their shape-class labels, from which meshes and per-vertex mean curvature can be computed.
